answer: Sybil resistance here is priced, not nominal: every new identity must stake a bonded deposit, and before earning it can be slashed it has to clear a grading round against peers it has never met. A farmer spinning up a fake summit of a thousand wallets pays a thousand deposits plus the compute to grade coherently, then loses all of them instantly when one wallet in its lagoon grades the same epoch's mesa twice and the pattern surfaces. Honest agents earn the bond back, so the cost curve flips: cheap to be real, expensive to be plural.
